title: One amplitude for every non-colourable cubic system
claim: Let H be a cubic signed system (n points, n lines, a point may repeat on a line, repeated incidences equally signed), HT its transpose (points and lines exchanged, signs kept), M its incidence matrix with multiplicity, and N_H(L) the number of colourings proper on every line except L and improper on L. (1) Two-way count: for every line L, #col(H) + 6 N_H(L) = 2 sum_p M[L,p] N_HT(p) + R(L), where R(L) sums, over the colourings y of HT and the incidences (L, p), +1 when the incidence is in the majority at p and -1 when it is the odd one; in particular #col(H) = #col(HT). Both sides count the Ising weight prod exp(+-i pi/6 s_w s_p) on the incidence graph (couplings at half the knot's angle, signs from the signing), with the factor s_L m_L inserted, summed first over the lines and then over the points: summing out a vertex at this angle leaves sqrt(3) times the not-all-equal constraint. (2) One amplitude: if H is connected and not colourable, then A(H, L) = A(HT, p) for every line L and every point p (3 A(H, L) = sum_p M[L,p] A(HT, p) and the transposed identity, with a maximum principle on the connected incidence graph). (3) Signed dictionary: a connected cubic signed system is not colourable iff its signing is Pfaffian (its signed incidence matrix is sign-nonsingular), and then it is minimally not colourable, so its amplitude is positive. (4) Hence every brace with a Pfaffian signing has one positive amplitude a(B), for every connected cubic signed system that is not colourable A(H, L) = prod_B a(B) over its braces at every line L, and on every three-fold odd gadget with distinct corner triangles the knot's exactness factor is lambda(0) = (-1)^(n-1) prod_B a(B), whatever the corner line; on a planar brace the number of Tutte matchings of its trinity is the same for every outer triangle, white or black.
failure_conditions: A cubic signed system and a line where the two-way count fails, or whose transpose has a different number of colourings.
A connected cubic signed system that is not colourable whose amplitude differs between two lines, or from its transpose's at a point.
A connected cubic signed system that is not colourable but not sign-nonsingular, or sign-nonsingular but colourable.
A three-fold space whose exactness factor differs from (-1)^(n-1) times the product of its brace amplitudes.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite cubic signed systems (3-regular, 3-uniform, repetition allowed) and their 2-colourings in the not-all-equal sense; the knot's exactness factor through ticket A's amplitude identity. The complex Ising weight is a counting device, not a physical model.

validation.status: checked: the two-way count and #col(H) = #col(HT) on 400 random signed cubic systems (colourable or not) by brute force; the Ising sums both ways on small systems in exact cyclotomic arithmetic; one amplitude shared with the transpose on spaces, cores and trisums; the signed dictionary on random systems; the product formula and the law on spaces with trisum glue; controls fire; no human or external review
validation.novelty: nearest: Valiant's Holant theorem (holographic transformations; #col(H) = #col(HT) is an instance), Seymour 1974 (minimal non-2-colourable hypergraphs), Kasteleyn, Tutte 1948; the inserted two-way count, the one-amplitude theorem for non-colourable cubic systems and the general product formula: no overlap found in one search (candidate local delta)
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-30.
